title: Revisiting Automatic Pipelining: Gate-level Forwarding and Speculation
problem: Pipelined processors suffer data hazards from read-after-write dependencies that cause stalls. Traditional high-level dataflow analysis for forwarding and speculation misses optimization opportunities embedded in gate-level netlist structures.
motivation: Optimizing pipeline throughput through better hazard resolution is fundamental to processor performance.
method: This approach looks at the detailed hardware circuit designs (gate-level netlist) instead of just analyzing how data flows between instructions. By examining these circuit patterns, it discovers additional opportunities to forward data between pipeline stages or predict future values before they're computed. These two techniques—forwarding and speculation—reduce the waiting periods (stalls) that occur when one instruction depends on another's result, making the automatic pipeline much more efficient.
key_novelty: The approach achieves more efficient pipelining by examining actual circuit structures (gate-level) to identify additional opportunities for data forwarding and prediction (speculation), rather than relying solely on high-level data flow analysis.
contributions: Gate-level netlist analysis framework for identifying pipeline optimization opportunities
Enhanced forwarding logic based on circuit-level structural analysis
Improved speculation techniques leveraging detailed hardware implementation details
Automatic pipelining methodology incorporating gate-level insights
